chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani, from Suleiman ibn Dawud al-Manqari, from Sufyan ibn Ayyinah, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

I found that all the knowledge of the people is in four areas: the first is to know your Lord; the second is to know what He has done with you; the third is to know what He wants from you; and the fourth is to know what will take you out of your religion.

key_terms.يُخْرِجُكَ مِنْ دِينِكَ: What takes you out of your religion

ai.seo_question: What are the four essential areas of knowledge according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), framing epistemology within a Shia theological context where self-knowledge is intrinsically linked to knowing the Creator. This four-part structure moves from ontological recognition of God to practical discernment of divine will and the specific mechanisms of spiritual deviation, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *ma'rifah* (gnosis) as the foundation of faith. The final pillar highlights the need for vigilance against internal and external factors that sever one's connection to the divine path.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-87 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani, on the authority of Suleiman ibn Davood al-Minqari, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Ayyineh that he had heard AbaAbdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) say,

“I found that all the knowledge of the people is in four areas:1- to know your Lord;2- to know what He has done with you;3- to know what He expects of you; and4- to know what will deviate you from your religion.”
